- [IARC.1.13] **Per-object allocation; no arena.**
  Every libds struct has `ds_<type>_new(engine, ...)`
  that allocates and `ds_<type>_free(obj)` that frees.
  No bulk arena allocation, no copy-on-write. Exactly one
  owner at any time; explicit ownership transfer where
  needed (documented per-function in headers, never
  implicit). Reference counting is used in two places and
  no others: the intern table's counted entries
  ([IDAT.4.7]), and the immutable structures a clone shares
  with its source ([IARC.11.1]).

  Rete-network memory — fact storage in working memory,
  alpha/beta-node state, tokens — is owned by the `rete`
  and `wm` modules and follows the same per-object
  discipline; it routes through the `DS_*` allocation
  macros ([IALC.1]) like all libds allocation.

  **OOM surfaces via `ds_result_t`.** Allocation
  failure returns a `DS_ERR_OOM` status through the
  standard result path ([IARC.1.12]); libds never
  aborts on OOM. Callers clean up anything partially
  constructed and propagate the failure. No
  try / rescue / `longjmp`.

  Rationale: simple to reason about, trivially
  profilable with standard heap tools (valgrind,
  Massif, tcmalloc hooks). At v1 fact / activation
  footprints (hundreds to low
  thousands active) allocation churn is a third-order
  concern. Arena-style escape hatches are reserved
  for specific hot paths if profiling warrants, not
  a global policy.
